text:
The contract stank. As a skipper, you said so.

That got you busted to navigation. Your first officer got your Wolf. You got a cell on Tapper�s flagship until the raid on Nachiketa was done.

From your cell you smelled fresh hull paint and listened to the guards complain. Weeks of boredom� followed by helpless terror.

The last hours are just fragments blurred by cryosleep.

Alarms. Explosions. Darkness. Smoke and so many screams�

Your marine officer in the doorway. A scramble in zero-g to a docked Hound, already filling with crew�

A titanic flash over Nachiketa. The jump to hyperspace�

Ruptured fuel tanks. Cryopods...

Nothing�

The Wolf and the Hound drifted together somehow. You set the course. Rolled the dice. Drifted into an abandoned system. Luck held. Barely.

You woke to alarms. Not battle�systems failing.

Cryopods kept most of you alive. Everything else fell apart. With life support failing, you had hours at best.

Two worlds with ruins. No time. You put people planetside. Engineers attempted repairs.

Days have passed. You finally have the drives online, but no fuel.

There�s too many survivors for life support to handle. People are staying behind.

You have tiny settlements on two planets. 
One green, alive, and trying to kill you in a thousand ways.
The other dry, hot, and rich enough to matter.
Between them, it should be enough.

For now.

The contract stank. Nachiketa was a bust. Tapper abandoned all of you.

Time to look to the future. People are depending on you to get them home.

Three priorities now:
There�s a comm relay in-system you could bring online.
Check on your people. See what they�ve scrounged.
And then�

Decide what happens next.

id: # --- Omicron array drone screens: dialog-layer defenders (Domain survey-ship pattern). The buoys are never destroyed; beating the screen unlocks the stock objective interaction until $defenderFleetDefeated expires (~30d). ---

text: Your sensors paint a lattice of dormant drones clamped to the buoy's mounting frame. As your $shipOrFleet closes, they detach in perfect unison and slide into an interdiction formation between you and the array. No warning is broadcast. The machines are simply waiting.

script:
ShowDefaultVisual
FireAll COB_AddOptions
FireBest COB_DisableOptionsIfNeeded
FireAll COB_DisableIndividualOptions

text: The drone screen accelerates in eerie synchrony, weapons charging as one.

The last drone tumbles away in fragments, and the buoy's interface accepts your handshake without complaint — the machine does not appear to hold grudges. Its replacement screen is doubtless already being assembled.

text:
The link opens on a $faction $post who does not bother to straighten up. "Heave to. This volume is under wartime interdiction and every hull in it gets looked over."

$HeOrShe glances at something off-image. "Or we skip the search. $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS credits says your holds are clean and I never saw you."

script:
$entity.ignorePlayerCommRequests = true 7
$exiles_hl_price = $entity.exiles_hl_toll 0
$exiles_hl_priceDGS = $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS 0
$exiles_hl_supplyPrice = $entity.exiles_hl_supplies 0
SetTextHighlights $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS
MakeOtherFleetPreventDisengage exileHLStop false
FireAll ExileHLStopOptions
text:
The link opens on a $faction $post whose eyes keep drifting to a tactical display. "This volume is under wartime interdiction. All traffic is subject to search."

A pause. "A contribution of $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS credits would settle the matter." It sounds more like a question than a demand.

"Unidentified fleet, this is the Hegemony Navy." The $post reads from a slate without looking up. "This port is under blockade by order of the High Hegemon. All traffic will stand by for inspection."

"The inspection fee is $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS credits if you want it done today. Otherwise my teams will take the time they need."

text:
"Unidentified fleet, this is the Hegemony Navy." The $post is very careful with $hisOrHer words. "This port is under blockade by order of the High Hegemon. You are requested to stand by for inspection."

"An inspection fee of $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS credits would expedite matters."

"This is a Persean League customs action." The $post smiles the way a clerk smiles at a queue. "Approach to this port is restricted for the duration of the emergency. Unlicensed traffic is held for examination."

"A transit licence is $entity.exiles_hl_tollDGS credits, payable now. Or you may wait for the examination."

text:
The boarding teams take their time. Hatches are opened that have not been opened in years, manifests are read line by line, and nothing is put back where it was found.

"You are free to go," the $post says at last, already looking at the next contact.

text: A shuttle comes alongside and leaves heavier than it arrived. "That will do," the $post says. "Safe flying."
There is a short delay while a registry is consulted. "So you do." The $post nods. "Carry on, $playerName."
The $post checks something, and $hisOrHer manner changes. "Understood. We were not informed. You may proceed."
The codes are received and, after a moment, accepted. "Your authorization is in order," the $post says. "You may proceed."
The $post looks you over again, and something like recognition arrives. "For you, $entity.exiles_hl_tollHalfDGS. That is as far as I go."
The $post frowns at a display, then at you, then at the display again. "Nobody tells me anything. Fine. Go."

text:
"Authority." The $post tastes the word. "My authority is the guns you are looking at. Nobody at home is going to ask what happened to one more trader out here."

It occurs to you that the same is true in the other direction.
"Your objection is noted and will be entered in the record," the $post says, without interest. "The order stands. You will comply, or you will be treated as a blockade runner."
The $post's face goes still. "On reflection, your papers appear to be in order." $HeOrShe will remember this. "Proceed."
